summary: Race condition in `tokio::time::Interval` on Tokio v1.54.0
details:
## Summary

On the multi-threaded runtime, there is a race condition between `Interval::poll_tick` and the runtime's time driver.

This affects `Interval` only. `Sleep` and `Timeout` are **not** affected.

## Details

In Tokio v1.54.0, a race condition between `tokio::time::Interval::poll_tick` (including `.tick().await`) and the runtime time driver can drop an internal timer entry without synchronizing with the driver thread that is firing it. This causes a data race and use-after-free on the timer's waker and task state in safe Rust, leading to assertion panics, task reference-count corruption, or heap memory corruption.

This bug was introduced by https://github.com/tokio-rs/tokio/pull/8458, and it was fixed by https://github.com/tokio-rs/tokio/pull/8692.

## Impact

This may lead to crashes and use-after-frees in applications using `Interval` on a multi-threaded runtime.

Since this issue is known to lead to crashes in production systems, the v1.54.0 release of Tokio has been yanked.

## Credits

Thank you to [creepycode](https://github.com/ByteZ1337) and [carabistouille](https://github.com/carabistouflette) for reporting this privately using the procedure outlined in our security policy. They both reported the issue independently of each other.

notes.text:
The monitoring functionality of affected CODESYS Control runtime systems processes read and write requests to PLC application data sent by the CODESYS Development System and other clients such as HMIs.

Due to improper synchronization in the CmpMonitor2 component when processing concurrent requests from multiple clients, incorrect data may be read or written, potentially resulting in unexpected behavior of the affected product. 

PLCs based on the CODESYS Runtime Toolkit or CODESYS Safety SIL2 are affected if they allow simultaneous access by two or more clients via the CODESYS protocol. In CODESYS Development System 3, simultaneous access to the included Simulation Runtime can only occur when access by an external client, such as an HMI, has been explicitly enabled through dedicated configuration. The default configuration of CODESYS Development System 3 is not affected.

The vulnerability can be exploited by an authenticated remote attacker with monitoring access by issuing concurrent requests to an affected product.

Oracle heeft meerdere kwetsbaarheden verholpen in diverse producten, waaronder Oracle SOA Suite, Oracle WebLogic Server, Oracle Data Integrator, Oracle Identity Manager, Oracle Access Manager, Oracle WebCenter Content, Oracle Fusion Middleware (inclusief Helidon) en Oracle HTTP Server.
notes.title: Feiten

notes.text:
De kwetsbaarheden betreffen onder andere onveilige deserialisatie, onvoldoende authenticatie- en toegangscontroles, kwetsbaarheden in netwerkprotocollen zoals HTTP, HTTP/2, SOAP, T3, IIOP en LDAP, en fouten in cryptografische bibliotheken zoals Bouncy Castle en Jackson-databind. Aanvallers kunnen hierdoor onder meer:

- Arbitrary code execution uitvoeren via crafted input of deserialisatieprocessen.
- Volledige systeemcompromittering bereiken via netwerktoegang zonder authenticatie.
- Ongeautoriseerde toegang verkrijgen tot gevoelige of kritieke data.
- Data manipuleren, creëren, verwijderen of wijzigen zonder juiste rechten.
- Denial-of-Service veroorzaken door resource-uitputting, crashes of hangs.
- Privilege escalation uitvoeren binnen het systeem.
- Cross-site scripting en spoofing aanvallen uitvoeren.
- Kwetsbaarheden in authenticatie- en autorisatiemechanismen misbruiken.

De kwetsbaarheden zijn aanwezig in specifieke versies van de genoemde Oracle producten en sommige onderliggende open source componenten die Oracle gebruikt. Exploitatie kan plaatsvinden via netwerktoegang, vaak zonder authenticatie, en in sommige gevallen is gebruikersinteractie vereist. Diverse kwetsbaarheden hebben een CVSS score tot 10.0, wat duidt op een hoog potentieel impactniveau. Er is (nog) geen specifieke proof-of-concept-code (PoC) bekend, maar de aard van de kwetsbaarheden maakt exploitatie mogelijk via gerichte netwerkverzoeken of gemanipuleerde data en het NCSC verwacht, vanwege de wijde verspreiding van deze producten, op korte termijn een toename in scan- en misbruikverkeer.

notes.text: Oracle heeft updates en patches uitgebracht voor de getroffen producten om de beschreven kwetsbaarheden te verhelpen. Gebruikers van de genoemde Oracle producten wordt geadviseerd de beschikbare updates te installeren om de beveiliging van hun systemen te waarborgen. Zie bijgevoegde referenties voor meer informatie.

descriptions.value: Ghidra versions through 12.1.4 contain a stack-based out-of-bounds write vulnerability in the decompiler's leftshift128 function when processing negative shift amounts from p-code. Attackers can craft malicious binaries with specific instruction sequences that trigger the overflow when decompiled, corrupting memory and potentially achieving code execution.

descriptions.value: Ghidra versions through 12.1.4 contain a heap use-after-free vulnerability in the decompiler's Funcdata::opInsertAfter function caused by stale INDIRECT effect-op references. Attackers can craft a malicious binary with a specific x86-64 sequence that triggers the vulnerability during decompilation, causing the decompile helper process to crash and denying service to analysts and automated analysis pipelines.

descriptions.value: webpack-dev-server is a development server that provides live reloading for webpack projects. In versions from 5.1.0 before 5.2.7 and in version 6.0.0, the unauthenticated open-editor endpoint validates the Host header with a regular expression meant for browser Origin schemes, so a Host value beginning with file: or with an extension scheme short-circuits the hostname and allowedHosts checks. A network peer that can reach the dev server can send a request with a malformed Host that passes validation and then causes the endpoint's URL construction to throw, and in the default non-production mode the server returns an HTTP 500 body containing the full exception stack trace, which discloses absolute filesystem paths, installed module locations, and internal source line numbers. The server keeps running, so there is no denial of service. The issue is fixed in webpack-dev-server 5.2.7 and 6.1.0, and users should upgrade to one of those versions or later.

descriptions.value: webpack-dev-server is a development server that provides live reloading for webpack projects. In versions before 5.2.7 and in version 6.0.0, when a proxy entry is configured to forward WebSockets, the server forwards non-HMR WebSocket upgrade requests to the proxy target without validating the Host or Origin headers, so the allowedHosts protection does not apply to those proxied upgrades. A malicious web page visited by a developer can open a cross-origin WebSocket through the dev server and read from and write to the proxied backend, even when the server is bound to loopback. The issue is fixed in webpack-dev-server 5.2.7 and 6.1.0, where proxied WebSocket upgrades pass the same Host and Origin validation as the HMR WebSocket, and users should upgrade to one of those versions or later. As a workaround, omit WebSocket forwarding from proxy entries that do not need it and scope the proxy to specific paths.

Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling vulnerability in esaml in dropbox esaml allows an unauthenticated attacker to exhaust the Erlang VM atom table and crash the node via unsigned LogoutResponse messages.

esaml:status_code_map/1 in src/esaml.erl maps any StatusCode value it does not recognize to an atom with list_to_atom/1 on the last colon-separated segment of the URN. esaml_sp:validate_logout_response/2 verifies a signature only when the message carries one, so an unsigned LogoutResponse posted to the single-logout endpoint reaches esaml:decode_logout_response/1 and mints one permanent atom per distinct status value. Atoms are never reclaimed and the VM caps the atom table at about one million entries, so an attacker who posts that many distinct values aborts the node.

This issue affects esaml: from 0.1.0 onward.

Improper Handling of Highly Compressed Data (Data Amplification) in esaml_binding in dropbox esaml allows an unauthenticated attacker to exhaust server memory and crash the Erlang VM via a crafted compressed SAMLResponse.

esaml_binding:decode_response/2 base64-decodes the attacker-supplied SAMLResponse, inflates it with zlib:unzip/1 with no bound on the output, then converts the result to a charlist with binary_to_list/1 before parsing. This runs on the SAML consume (ACS) and single-logout endpoints, which accept unauthenticated requests by design, and it runs before any signature check. A small deflate stream reaches a compression ratio near 1000 to 1, so a request body of tens of kilobytes inflates to hundreds of megabytes and then to several gigabytes of list heap, so a few requests exhaust memory and take the node down.

This issue affects esaml: from 0.1.0 onward.

A flaw was found in mod_qos. An unauthenticated remote attacker could cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by sending a specially crafted JSON request when JSON body filtering is enabled. Due to improper string termination during the processing of percent-encoded input, the module reads past allocated memory boundaries, which can cause an Apache worker process to crash.

A flaw was found in mod_qos. An unauthenticated remote attacker can cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by maintaining numerous concurrent low-rate connections to a target server. When connection rate monitoring is active, the module fails to verify array boundaries when recording client IP addresses, allowing more connection records to be added than the allocated buffer can hold. This issue leads to heap memory corruption, which can crash the web server process.
